entries.gap: KLU fails on a large mixed deck (17 block instances, HBT and PSP MOS): the singular pivots change from run to run (PSP noise nodes).
entries.symptom: The operating point falls back to a transient op and fails.
entries.workaround: Use the sparse solver (.options klu off) for whole-chip DC points. The same blocks pass with KLU alone.
entries.evidence: whole-chip DC point of a reference design (sparse passes at three corners, KLU fails)

entries.gap: Monte Carlo DC points with reltol 1e-4: 21 of 300 seeds need the transient-op fallback, 4 have no DC point from Newton. The cause is the solver, not the circuit.
entries.symptom: Seeds without a DC point, or fallback snapshots with large offsets.
entries.workaround: Use reltol=1e-3 and itl1=1000 for the operating points of a Monte Carlo run (300 of 300 seeds converge); state the options. The ngspice operation monte_carlo uses these options by default and reports a seed without a DC point (seeds_no_dc, work/mc.json); a monte_carlo requirement row is then not measured.
entries.evidence: Monte Carlo of an IF amplifier block of a reference design

entries.gap: The npn13G2 card has self-heating (selft=1) with a thermal time constant of about 5 ns.
entries.symptom: Transient values drift for tens of ns.
entries.workaround: Read transient results after more than 25 ns, or set selft=0 for method comparisons (state it).

entries.gap: The small-signal (AC) self-heating term of the npn13G2 card (VBIC selft=1, rth = 3.26e3 (4/Nx)^0.9 K/W, cth = 1.6e-12 (Nx/4)^0.95 J/K; thermal corner 1/(2 pi rth cth) about 33 MHz at Nx 1 and 31 MHz at Nx 4) has the wrong sign and size in ngspice. The DC result is right: at low frequency Re(y22) must equal the DC slope dIc/dVce. npn13G2 Nx 1, VBE 0.92 V, VCE 1.2 V (Ic 2.03 mA), tt 27 C: DC slope +453 uS (ngspice) and +450 uS (Xyce); Re(y22) at 1 kHz -291.8 uS in ngspice, +450.2 uS in Xyce. With selft=0 the two simulators agree (Re 1.52 uS, Im 24.46 uS at 1 GHz).
entries.symptom: No message. ngspice AC, .noise and S-parameter results of HBT circuits are wrong below about ten times the thermal corner (300 MHz): negative output conductance at low frequency, a wrong reactive term near the corner (Im y22 at 1 GHz: ngspice 30.3 uS, Xyce 13.9 uS, without self-heating 24.5 uS). ngspice 41 differs from 46. DC, transient and Xyce AC/HB agree with the DC slope.
entries.workaround: For AC, .noise and S-parameter rows below about 1 GHz (low-frequency stability and loop gain, bias loops, IF and baseband gain, low-frequency noise transfer), use Xyce AC/.noise for HBT-only decks, or an ngspice transient. selft=0 alone is not a fix: the DC point moves (1.62 mA against 2.03 mA in the test); selft=0 with a dtemp from the selft=1 DC point is not verified. Rows at the RF frequencies (tens of GHz), DC and transient results are not affected. A device check must compare the DC slope with low-frequency AC, and each decade up to the band of use.
entries.evidence: device sign test: DC slope from two DC points (VCE 1.19/1.20/1.21 V) against Re(y22) at 1 kHz, 1 MHz, 1 GHz, ngspice 46 and Xyce 7.10, with selft=1 and selft=0 (simulated); found as a y22 difference at 1 GHz in device_crosscheck (0.114 mS ngspice, 0.068 mS Xyce, Nx 4)

entries.gap: The antenna diode model has a jump near 3 n Vt (a discontinuity) that can stall transients of pad circuits.
entries.symptom: 'timestep too small' near zero diode voltage.
entries.workaround: Leave the pad antenna diodes out of the transient deck when the pad is not under test, and state it.
entries.evidence: pad circuit transients of an earlier design

entries.gap: In a transient, the VBIC instance vectors @q[ib] (and, to a smaller part, @q[ic]) of npn13G2 include the charge currents of the junction capacitances; they are not the conduction currents.
entries.symptom: A shot-noise PSD 2 q |i| from these vectors is too high: in a 61.8 GHz VCO the base shot noise was 24 dB and the collector shot noise 1.7 dB above the result with the conduction currents.
entries.workaround: Take the conduction currents from a DC table of the device at the junction voltages of the transient (@q[vbe], @q[vbc]): in the oscillator operation, isf.devices and shot {device, current}.
entries.evidence: simulated, ngspice 46: oscillator operation with shot vectors against the stored conduction-current result of the same deck; with isf.devices the result equals the stored result within 0.02 dB per source

entries.gap: The mismatch sections of the IHP corner libraries (<corner>_mismatch) give mismatch only to instances with mm_ok=1: each device subcircuit has mm_ok=0 by default, and a global .param mm_ok=1 does not change it.
entries.symptom: A Monte Carlo run in which every seed gives the same value, with no message: the offset looks like zero.
entries.workaround: Set mm_ok=1 on each PDK device instance, or use the ngspice operation monte_carlo, which adds it and fails when no measurement varies over the seeds.
entries.evidence: PDK libraries *_mod_mismatch.lib (agauss(..., (mm_ok != 1 ? 0 : 1))); a 60-seed run of a detector cell gives offset sigma 3.9 mV with mm_ok=1

entries.gap: The ngspice HBT subcircuits of the PDK set sw_nqs=0 by default, so the excess-phase delay td = sw_nqs x 0.28 ps is off. The Xyce card has td on (no sw_nqs parameter).
entries.symptom: No message. At 122.5 GHz one Nx 4 device (VBE 0.88 V, VCE 1.2 V) has y21 60.9 mS at -37.3 deg with the default and 62.97 mS at -45.1 deg in Xyce (13.7 % apart); with sw_nqs=1 the two agree within 1.2 %. ngspice and Xyce differ for the same netlist, and RF gain, phase, match, stability and oscillation frequency move.
entries.workaround: Set sw_nqs=1 on every HBT instance of an RF path in ngspice (instance parameter; no model card change). In a netlist gate, declare it: allow_params {"npn13g2": {"sw_nqs": [1]}} and, to enforce it, require_params {"npn13g2": {"sw_nqs": 1}}. To find such a difference before a design uses both simulators: xyce adapter, operation device_crosscheck, or the device_check gate of a requirements file.
entries.evidence: PDK files sg13g2_hbt_mod.lib (ngspice: sw_nqs=0 and td = sw_nqs*2.80E-13; Xyce: td = 2.80E-13); one-device y-parameters at 122.5 GHz in a reference design (ngspice default, ngspice sw_nqs=1, Xyce); task references run with both settings (evals lna-sg13g2 and vco-sg13g2, expected_nqs0.json against expected.json): LNA s22 at 122.5 GHz -10.18 to -8.84 dB, VCO phase noise at 1 MHz -87.96 to -89.89 dBc/Hz (tt) and -83.97 to -82.70 dBc/Hz (slow, 125 C); device_crosscheck in the environment image (test device-crosscheck-container). Open: with sw_nqs=1, y22 at 1 GHz is 0.114 mS in ngspice and 0.068 mS in Xyce (cause not known; both cards have self-heating on)
